user.title: Guided cover calibration
user.description:
This tool calibrates “basic” covers: the ones whose actuator does not report where it is. The percentage you see in Home Assistant for those is an estimate, computed from how long the motor has been running; the calibration measures those run times and the geometry of the roll, so that the estimate becomes one you can rely on.

It will not be perfect. Expect a few centimetres of error: 1-2 cm near the end stops, 2-4 cm between intermediate positions. Every full opening or closing re-synchronises the estimate, so the error does not accumulate.

“Advanced” covers report their own position and do not need any of this, which is why they are not in the list.

**What is about to happen**: you will pick one shutter, then one of three ways of measuring it. The shutter will run to its end stops several times.

**What you have to do**: have a tape measure to hand, make sure nothing is in the way of the shutter, and stay where you can see it. Nothing is saved until the very last screen, so you can close this window at any moment and nothing will have changed.

cover.title: Which shutter are we measuring?
cover.description:
Only the basic covers of this gateway are listed: the ones that do not report their own position, and are therefore the only ones with something to calibrate.

**What you have to do**: choose the shutter you are standing in front of. You will be asked to watch it move and to measure it with a tape, so it has to be the one you can see.

path.title: How should {cover} be measured?
path.description:
There are three ways to do this, and the right one depends on what you have measured already.

The first is the long one, about three minutes: three button presses and three readings with a tape. It ends with a **profile**, a description of this kind of shutter that every other window of the same model can reuse.

The second is for those other windows: pick the profile, measure the height, done.

The third is for a shutter that follows a profile and still stops in the wrong place.

**What you have to do**: pick one. Nothing moves until the next screen.

menu_options.path_a: This is the first shutter of its kind (full measurement, ~3 minutes)
menu_options.path_b: This one is the same as a shutter already measured (height only)
menu_options.path_c: This one follows a profile but stops in the wrong place (refine it)

path_a.title: Before {cover} starts moving
path_a.description:
**What is about to happen**: the shutter will run all the way down, then all the way up, then down again, and then to a few positions in between. Seven movements in all, about three minutes.

**What you have to do**: make sure nothing is in its way — no open window, no plant on the sill, no cat — and keep a tape measure to hand. You will be asked to press a button when something happens, and to read a few distances.

You can stop at any moment: nothing is written until the last screen, and the movements are ordinary commands.

path_b.title: Which kind of shutter is {cover}?
path_b.description:
A profile describes one model of shutter: how long it takes to run, how long the slats take, and how the curtain winds on its tube. Home Assistant scales it to this window once it knows how tall this window is.

**What you have to do**: pick the profile that was measured on a shutter of the same kind. On the next screen you will measure the height of this one.

path_c.title: Refine {cover}
path_c.description:
This shutter follows a profile and does not behave like it: its motor may be slower, its curtain heavier, its tube thicker. What is measured here is stored for this window alone and beats both the profile and myhome.yaml; everything that is not measured keeps coming from the profile.

**What you have to do**: confirm which profile this shutter should start from.

refine_scope.title: How far should {cover} be refined?
refine_scope.description:
**What is about to happen**: either two measured runs (one up, one down) or those plus two tape readings.

The times alone are enough for a shutter whose motor is simply slower or faster than the one the profile was measured on. Add the coefficients when it also stops in the wrong place *half way* — that is the curtain winding differently, not the motor running differently.

**What you have to do**: pick how far to go. You can always come back and do more.

menu_options.times_only: Its own run times (2 button presses, ~1 minute)
menu_options.times_and_rolls: Its own run times and its own coefficients (2 presses and 2 readings)

home_closed_done.title: Is {cover} fully closed?
home_closed_done.description:
**What has happened**: the shutter was sent all the way down, so that everything measured from now on starts from a known point.

**What you have to do**: look at it. If it is fully closed, with the slats shut and the bottom edge resting, carry on. If it is still moving, wait and then carry on. If it did not move at all, or moved the wrong way, say so below.

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

home_open_done.title: Is {cover} fully open?
home_open_done.description:
**What has happened**: the shutter was sent all the way up, because what follows runs downwards from there and a run that started anywhere else would measure nothing.

**What you have to do**: look at it. If it is fully open, carry on. If it is still moving, wait and then carry on. If it did not move at all, or moved the wrong way, say so below.

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_lift.title: {cover} is opening
open_lift.description:
**What is happening**: the shutter has started to rise. For the first second or two only the slats open, while the bottom edge stays on its rest; then the whole curtain begins to lift.

**What you have to do**: watch the bottom edge and press the button below **at the instant it leaves its rest**. Do not time anything — the press is the measurement, and Home Assistant knows exactly when the motor started.

Let the shutter carry on afterwards: it will run to the top on its own.

menu_options.lifted_off: The bottom edge has just lifted off
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_top.title: {cover} is still opening
open_top.description:
**What is happening**: the curtain is winding up and the shutter will stop by itself at the top.

**What you have to do**: press the button below **at the instant it stops**. If you missed the moment, repeat the step rather than guessing: the whole opening time comes from this press.

menu_options.stopped_open: It has just stopped at the top
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

close_bottom.title: {cover} is closing
close_bottom.description:
**What is happening**: the shutter was opened fully and is now running down. It will stop by itself when the curtain is down and the slats have closed.

**What you have to do**: press the button below **at the instant it stops**. That press is the whole closing time; a shutter closes a little faster than it opens, which is why it is measured separately.

menu_options.stopped_closed: It has just stopped at the bottom
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

height.title: How tall is {cover}?
height.description:
**What you have to do**: with the shutter fully open, measure from the point where the bottom edge rests when the shutter is closed up to the bottom edge as it is now, and write the centimetres below.

That distance is the travel of the curtain, and it is what every other measurement is compared against. Measure the curtain, not the window: if the bottom edge rests on a sill rather than on the floor, measure from the sill.

measure_descent.title: Measure {cover} — {percent}% of the way down
measure_descent.description:
**What has happened**: the shutter was opened fully and then run down for {percent}% of its travel.

**What you have to do**: measure again from the point where the bottom edge rests when the shutter is closed up to the bottom edge as it is now, and write the centimetres below. The same reference as the height, so the two can be compared.

data.repeat_step: Repeat this step instead (run its movements again and measure afresh)

measure_ascent.title: Measure {cover} — {percent}% of the way up
measure_ascent.description:
**What has happened**: the shutter was closed fully and then run up for the slats plus {percent}% of its travel.

**What you have to do**: measure from the point where the bottom edge rests when the shutter is closed up to the bottom edge as it is now, and write the centimetres below. A shutter is not equally loaded going up and going down, which is why the same fraction is measured twice.

data.repeat_step: Repeat this step instead (run its movements again and measure afresh)

measure_verify.title: Check {cover} — {percent}% of the way down
measure_verify.description:
**What has happened**: the shutter was run to a position nothing was measured at, so this is a real check and not a repetition.

**What you have to do**: measure the height of the bottom edge one last time, from the same reference as before, and write the centimetres below. The next screen says how far the shutter is from where Home Assistant thought it would be.

data.repeat_step: Repeat this step instead (run its movements again and measure afresh)

verify_offer.title: Would you like to check {cover}?
verify_offer.description:
The height is all that was needed, and the calibration can be saved as it is.

**What the check is**: the shutter is sent half way down and you measure where it really stopped, which says whether this window really behaves like the profile. It takes about a minute and one tape reading.

verify_result.title: {cover} stopped {deviation} cm from the estimate
verify_result.description:
That is the distance between where the shutter really stopped and where Home Assistant believed it would. One or two centimetres is as good as this gets; three or more means this window does not behave like the profile it was given.

**What you have to do**: carry on to the summary, measure the same position again if you think the reading was wrong, or refine this shutter with measurements of its own when the option is offered.

menu_options.path_c: Refine this shutter with its own measurements

summary.title: What was measured on {cover}

menu_options.refine: Improve the accuracy first (~2 minutes, 4 more readings)

profile_name.title: Name this kind of shutter
profile_name.description:
{cover} has been measured, and what was measured describes every window of the same model. Give that model a name and the other shutters can be calibrated in two screens instead of ten.

**What you have to do**: type a short name — letters, digits and underscores only, no spaces and no accents, because it is also a key in `myhome.yaml`. Something like `tall`, `bedrooms` or `kitchen_door`.

A name that is already in use is not refused: the profile of that name is **replaced** by what has just been measured, which is how a shutter whose first measurement was poor is measured again. A `cover_profiles:` block of the same name in `myhome.yaml` is left untouched and goes on being hidden behind the measured one.

reconfigure.title: Measure {cover} again
reconfigure.description:
This shutter already has a guided calibration. There is nothing in it worth editing by hand — every number came from a button press or a tape — so the way to change it is to measure it again.

**What is about to happen**: the same conversation as the first time. What is stored now stays exactly as it is until you reach the last screen and save.

problem_no_echo.title: {cover} did not answer
problem_no_echo.description:
The command reached the bus but the actuator never reported that it had started moving, so there is no instant to measure anything against and the step was abandoned.

**The shutter may still be moving**: the command did go out, so the motor has very probably started. A stop was sent straight after the failure, but if the shutter is still running, stop it yourself before repeating the step.

**What you have to do**: check that the shutter is not blocked, that nothing else (a wall switch, an automation) is holding it, and try the step again. If it happens every time, this actuator does not relay its status and the guided calibration cannot measure it.

problem_not_delivered.title: The command never reached the bus
problem_not_delivered.description:
The gateway neither wrote our command nor said it had given up on it, so {cover} was never asked to move and nothing was measured.

**What you have to do**: check that the gateway is connected — the integration page says so — and try the step again.

problem_not_stopped.title: {cover} could not be stopped
problem_not_stopped.description:
The stop command was refused or dropped, so the shutter ran on to its end stop and the position this step was about does not exist.

**What you have to do**: wait until the shutter is standing still and try the step again. A gateway that is busy with a great many commands is the usual reason.

problem_busy.title: {cover} is already moving
problem_busy.description:
A step has to start from a standstill, and this shutter was already running — somebody at a wall switch, an automation, or a command that had not finished.

**What you have to do**: wait until it has stopped, then try the step again.

problem_bad_point.title: Those two presses cannot both be right
problem_bad_point.description:
The instants do not make sense together: the shutter cannot have stopped before it started, nor have opened its slats after it had finished.

**What you have to do**: try the step again and press once for each event, as it happens.

problem_timeout.title: Nothing was pressed in time
problem_timeout.description:
This screen waits about a minute and a half for the press it is about, which is far longer than any shutter takes to run. Past that the press no longer measures anything, so it was discarded rather than believed.

**What you have to do**: try the step again, and this time press as soon as the shutter does what the screen describes.

problem_unknown.title: Something went wrong with {cover}
problem_unknown.description:
The step could not be completed and nothing was measured. The Home Assistant log has the detail.

**What you have to do**: try the step again. Nothing has been saved, whatever you choose.

progress.homing_closed: {cover} is being closed all the way, so that the measurements start from a known point. Please wait, and make sure nothing is in its way.
progress.homing_open: {cover} is being opened all the way, so that the movement that follows starts from a known point. Please wait, and make sure nothing is in its way.
progress.starting_open: {cover} is being closed all the way and then started upwards. Please wait: the next screen asks you to watch it and press a button.
progress.starting_close: {cover} is being opened all the way and then started downwards. Please wait: the next screen asks you to watch it and press a button.
progress.running_down: {cover} is being opened all the way and then run down to about {percent}% of its travel. Please wait, and have the tape measure ready.
progress.running_up: {cover} is being closed all the way and then run up to about {percent}% of its travel. Please wait, and have the tape measure ready.

error.invalid_name: A profile name may only contain letters, digits and underscores — no spaces, no accents, no dashes.
error.above_the_travel: That is more than the whole travel of this curtain. Measure from where the bottom edge rests when the shutter is closed, not from the floor.

abort.no_basic_covers: Every cover of this gateway reports its own position, so there is nothing to calibrate. The guided calibration is only for covers whose position Home Assistant has to estimate from run times.
abort.no_profiles: There is no profile to follow yet. Calibrate one shutter with the full measurement first: that is what creates a profile.
abort.unknown_cover: That cover is no longer part of this gateway's configuration. Nothing was measured and nothing was saved.
abort.already_calibrating: This shutter is already being calibrated: another dialog is open on it, or the cover_calibration_run service is driving it. Two calibrations on one motor would each measure a run the other one stopped, so this one was not started. Finish or close the other one and try again.
abort.cancelled: The calibration was cancelled. Nothing was saved and the shutter is where the last movement left it.
abort.calibration_saved: The calibration of {cover} has been saved. The shutter now uses the measured values, its attributes say so, and removing this entry from the integration page gives it back to myhome.yaml.

reconfigure.title: Profile “{profile}”

abort.add_profile_via_calibration: A profile is not typed in, it is measured. Run the guided calibration on the first shutter of a kind and choose “This is the first shutter of its kind”: the last screen asks for the name of the profile.

init.title: MyHome options
init.description: Connection and advanced settings. The integration is reloaded when you save.

data.generate_events: Generate events in Home Assistant for each message received

data_description.command_worker_count: How many command sessions the integration opens to the gateway. More sessions send queued commands in parallel, but gateways hold only a handful. Default 1 (1-4).
data_description.idle_watchdog_sec: No frame received on the monitor session for this long: a harmless probe is sent through the command session. Default 300 s (60-3600).
data_description.probe_window_sec: How long the probe is given to be answered. If nothing arrives on the monitor session and the gateway acknowledges no status request on the command session within this time, the connection is rebuilt. Default 30 s (5-300).
data_description.command_timeout_sec: How long a single command may take to be written and acknowledged before it is retried once and then dropped. Default 10 s (2-60).
data_description.queue_ttl_sec: Commands still queued after this long are dropped instead of being sent late. Default 60 s (10-600).
data_description.default_keepalive_minutes: Keep-alive requested from the energy meters when keepalive_minutes is set neither on the sensor nor in the gateway's sensor_defaults: block (alias energy:) of myhome.yaml. 0 disables it. Default 125 min (0-255).

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

start_sending_instant_power.name: Start sending instant power
start_sending_instant_power.description: Asks the energy meter of the targeted power sensors to send instant power updates.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: For how many minutes (1-255) the instant power updates are sent. Defaults to the sensor's keepalive_minutes.

start_discovery.name: Start device discovery
start_discovery.description: Listens to the bus for 60 seconds and writes YAML suggestions for unknown devices to myhome_discovered.yaml.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

stop_discovery.name: Stop device discovery
stop_discovery.description: Stops a running device discovery and writes the suggestions collected so far.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

cover_calibration_run.name: Calibrate cover (run)
cover_calibration_run.description: Sends the cover to one end, then runs it for exactly the motor time a set_cover_position 50 would use with its current configuration and stops it there, so the height of the bar can be measured for cover_calibration_compute.

direction.name: Direction
direction.description: Which run to measure: 'close' starts from fully open and runs half the curtain time, 'open' starts from fully closed and runs the slat time plus half the curtain time.

cover_calibration_compute.name: Calibrate cover (compute)
cover_calibration_compute.description: Turns the heights measured after cover_calibration_run into the roll of this cover - one per direction when both runs were measured - and returns a cover_profiles snippet ready to paste into myhome.yaml.

height.name: Curtain travel
height.description: Distance in centimetres between the fully open and the fully closed bar (the travel, not the window).

closed_half_cm.name: Height after the closing half run
closed_half_cm.description: Centimetres between the floor and the bottom of the bar, measured after cover_calibration_run with direction 'close'.

opened_half_cm.name: Height after the opening half run
opened_half_cm.description: The same measurement after direction 'open'. Optional: it is what gives the separate opening_roll, and without it only the closing roll is worked out.

slat_time.name: Slat time
slat_time.description: Seconds of slat-only travel. It is an input, never an answer: given here it is used as it stands, otherwise the value configured on the cover is.

closed_run_seconds.name: Closing run length
closed_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the closing run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.

opened_run_seconds.name: Opening run length
opened_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the opening run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.
